title: Agentic Framework for Epidemiological Modeling
claim: A scenario specification and prompt flow through an abstract intermediate graph into executable simulator code, then verification feedback loops back to refine it.
layout: 4 panels, left-to-right, with a feedback arrow looping back under the last panel
description: Four rounded panels run left to right, linked by blue arrows. Panel 1 (green dotted border) shows a scenario table of vaccination policy against immune escape, labeled Scenarios A to E, plus a Prompt note box that defines the compartments S, E and I. Panel 2 (gray) holds a Prompt box, a small node-and-edge Epi Graph, and a Skeleton Code snippet with a TODO. Panel 3 (dotted maroon border) shows PyTorch simulator code above a line plot of predicted and ground-truth cumulative infections, labeled Simulator and Trajectories. Panel 4 (purple border) has a Prompt box and a Verification Steps checklist labeled V&V Feedback. A large blue arrow curves back leftward beneath it to show the feedback loop. Underlined blue labels name each element. The eye goes first to the scenario table, then follows the arrows.
caption: Data flow in \tool{} has the following structure: Prompt $\;\leftrightarrow\;$ Flow Graph $\;\rightarrow\;$ Simulator Code $\;\rightarrow\;$ Results. The flow graph is an abstract representation of the epidemic model being learned, and supports easier verification. The flow graph is then transformed into the actual epidemic model and is calibrated, and fully verified. The components here map to those in the architecture of \tool{}, shown in Figure [ref].
abstract: Epidemic modeling is essential for public health planning, yet traditional approaches rely on fixed model classes that require manual redesign as pathogens, policies, and scenario assumptions evolve. We introduce EPIAGENT, an agentic framework that automatically synthesizes, calibrates, verifies, and refines epidemiological simulators by modeling disease progression as an iterative program synthesis problem. A central design choice is an explicit epidemiological flow graph intermediate representation that links scenario specifications to model structure and enables strong, modular correctness checks before code is generated. Verified flow graphs are then compiled into mechanistic models supporting interpretable parameter learning under physical and epidemiological constraints. Evaluation on epidemiological scenario case studies demonstrates that EPIAGENT captures complex growth dynamics and produces epidemiologically consistent counterfactual projections across varying vaccination and immune escape assumptions. Our results show that the agentic feedback loop prevents degeneration and significantly accelerates convergence toward valid models by mimicking professional expert workflows.
